mercy_translation.text:
Someone may say: he ought to have hidden from the plot of the Jews in order to preserve his body altogether immortal. Let such a person hear that this too would have been unfitting for the Lord. Just as it was not fitting for the Word of God, who is Life, to give death to his own body from himself, so neither was it fitting for him to flee the death given by others. Rather, it was fitting that he pursue it toward its destruction. Therefore he neither laid aside the body by himself nor fled from the Jews who plotted against him.

This did not show weakness in the Word. Rather, it made him known as Savior and Life: he awaited death in order to abolish it and hastened to complete the death offered to him for the salvation of all.

Moreover, the Savior did not come to complete his own death but the death of human beings. Therefore he did not lay aside the body by a death proper to himself—for as Life he had no such death—but he received the death that came from human beings so that, when it approached him in his own body, he might completely destroy it.

From the following considerations one may also reasonably see why the Lord's body had such an end. The Lord cared especially about the resurrection of the body that he was going to accomplish. For this was his trophy over death: to show the resurrection to all, to assure everyone of the abolition of corruption accomplished by him, and thereafter of the incorruption of bodies. As a pledge and sign of the resurrection that is to come upon all, he preserved his own body incorruptible.

If, on the other hand, the body had fallen sick and the Word had departed from it in the sight of all, it would have been unfitting that the One who healed the diseases of others should neglect his own instrument as it wasted away in disease. How would he have been believed to drive away the weaknesses of others if his own temple in him were weak? Either he would have been mocked as unable to drive away disease, or, if able yet unwilling, he would have been thought lacking in love toward others as well.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
Athanasius argues that Christ receives death from others rather than dying from disease or natural weakness so that his victory over death can be publicly manifested.
The body is called Christ's temple and instrument, consistent with Athanasius' earlier language.
